result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by narrow, poorly maintained sidewalks on one side and a lack of paved walkways on the other. The roadway shows significant pavement degradation and lacks marked crossings or traffic calming measures, creating a hostile environment for pedestrians in a residential area.

hazards.name: Missing/Degraded Sidewalk
hazards.description: The right side of the street lacks a continuous paved walkway, forcing pedestrians to walk in the roadway or on uneven dirt/grass.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway along the property lines

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash bins and debris are placed on the already narrow sidewalk, further restricting pedestrian movement.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground on the sidewalk near the red car

hazards.name: Poor Roadway Condition
hazards.description: Significant cracking and uneven pavement surfaces create trip hazards and may affect vehicle control.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion and Repair
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant paved sidewalk on both sides of the street to provide safe pedestrian separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks with compliant curb ramps to provide designated and accessible crossing points.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or chicanes to reduce vehicle speeds in this residential context.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a narrow sidewalk adjacent to a large blank wall and informal parking. A large van in the foreground significantly obstructs sightlines between pedestrians and potential vehicle traffic, creating a hazardous crossing environment.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicle
hazards.description: A large green van is parked immediately adjacent to the walkway, completely blocking the view of the street for pedestrians and the view of pedestrians for drivers.

hazards.name: Blank Wall Frontage
hazards.description: A long, high blank wall creates a dead space with no passive surveillance, which can decrease the perceived and actual safety of pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center, below the grocery store sign

interventions.title: Daylighting at Intersections and Access Points
interventions.description: Remove parking near the driveway and alley entrance to improve sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Install a planting strip or street trees to provide physical and psychological separation between the sidewalk and the roadway.

interventions.title: Active Frontage Improvements
interventions.description: Incorporate windows or public art/murals on the blank wall to improve the pedestrian experience and sense of safety through increased visual interest.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with continuous sidewalks and a marked crosswalk at a stop-controlled intersection. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the environment lacks buffers between the walkway and parked vehicles, and sightlines at the crossing are potentially obscured by on-street parking.

hazards.name: Visibility Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners may block sightlines between approaching drivers and pedestrians attempting to use the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs approaching the marked crosswalk at the intersection.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and physically prevent parking too close to the crosswalk.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a continuous but narrow sidewalk that lacks a buffer from the roadway. The pedestrian environment is constrained by utility poles and mature trees, with on-street parallel parking further narrowing the effective visual field.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A utility pole is located directly in the path of the narrow sidewalk, significantly reducing the clear width for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image on the sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is immediately adjacent to the curb with no physical separation or planting strip to buffer pedestrians from moving traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire visible sidewalk edge

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: Visible cracking and uneven surfaces on the sidewalk and roadway can create tripping hazards.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Expand the sidewalk width to ensure a consistent clear path of at least 5 feet, especially around utility poles.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Install a planting strip or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a safety buffer from vehicles.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at nearby intersections to improve visibility and shorten crossing distances.
